```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
```

`simregdata` returns simulated CBS microdata through a drop-in `read_sav()`.
Code written against it runs unchanged in CBS Remote Access, where the same
call reads the real file.

## Read a file

```{r init}
library(haven)
library(simregdata)  # after haven, so read_sav() is the simulator's

sim_init("woonbase", year = 2023, n = 5000, seed = 42)

pers <- read_sav("WoonbasePopulatiePersonen2023V1",
                 col_select = c(RINPERSOON, HUISHOUDNR1Jan, TYPHH1Jan))
head(pers)
```

`sim_init()` builds a shared population *spine* of persons, households and
dwellings; every dataset draws from it. `sim_catalog()` lists all file names.

## Labels and codes

Categorical columns are `haven::labelled`, as in real `.sav` files.
`cbs_code()` recovers the original CBS character codes:

```{r labels}
table(as_factor(pers$TYPHH1Jan))

sim_init("rdw", year = 2023)
rdw <- read_sav("RDWNPACT2023TABV1", n_max = 5)
cbs_code(rdw$BRANDSTCODECORVRTG)
```

## Joins across files

Identifiers (`RINPERSOON`, `HUISHOUDNR`, `RINOBJECTNUMMER`, `RINPERSOONHKW`)
come from the spine, so joins between datasets match as on the real data:

```{r joins}
sim_init("inpatab", year = 2023)
inpa <- read_sav("INPA2023TABV1", col_select = c(RINPERSOON, INPPERSBESTINK))

joined <- merge(pers, inpa, by = "RINPERSOON")
nrow(joined) / nrow(pers)
```

## Export to parquet

For larger runs, `sim_population()` writes a sample of the population to
parquet in the CBS folder layout; `sim_set_data_root()` then makes
`read_sav()` read those files instead of simulating:

```r
sim_population("sim_data", datasets = c("woonbase", "rdw"),
               years = 2019:2023, fraction = 0.01)
sim_set_data_root("sim_data")
```

`sim_scan_columns()` finds the `col_select` columns your scripts use, so the
export only writes what you need.

## Other files

`read_sav()` passes any name it does not recognise to `haven::read_sav()`,
so one call works for simulated and real files. Datasets of your own can be
added from a YAML file with `sim_create_custom()` and `sim_register()`.

## How it works

Each dataset is defined in YAML under `inst/config/datasets/`: a manifest,
codelists, column definitions and year-specific parameters. The parameters
are calibrated to CBS StatLine and stored in the package, so generating data
needs no network. The `*_update_params()` functions refresh them.

Persons have a deterministic life course (birth, death, migration), so the
population changes between years while identifiers stay stable. Building the
spine for one million persons takes about 10 seconds.

Results on simulated data are for checking code, not for interpretation.
The worked examples, starting with `vignette("quality-cars")`, show which
results look like the published statistics and what changes in Remote
Access. See the
[provenance article](https://joris-klingen.github.io/simregdata/articles/provenance.html)
for where each parameter comes from.
